name: passwd
description: Changes user passwords and password policies (expiry, lock state).

flags.description: Change your own password (prompts for the current one).
As root: change another user's password without knowing the old one.
Lock / unlock a password (same effect as usermod -L/-U).
Show password status: set, locked, or empty.
Force the password to expire at next login.

examples.output:
Changing password for user.
Current password: 
New password:
examples.explanation: Changes your own password. Weak passwords are rejected if they are too short, dictionary-based, or similar to the old one (PAM policy).
As root, resets alice's password without knowing the previous one — the standard "forgot password" recovery.
Status: P = password set, L = locked, NP = no password.
Forces alice to choose a new password at her next login — standard practice for initial accounts.

about: passwd writes the (hashed) password to /etc/shadow, which only root can read. Password quality is enforced by PAM modules (pam_pwquality on most modern distros). Hashing defaults to yescrypt on Debian 11+/Ubuntu 22+ and SHA-512 elsewhere.
useCases: Reset a forgotten user password as admin.
mistakes: Typing the password on the command line (e.g. echo pass | passwd) — it leaks into shell history; always use the interactive prompt.
warnings: passwd -d removes the password entirely, allowing passwordless login on some configurations. Never use it on real accounts.
